findings.evidence: grep of TauCeti/Analysis/Fredholm/Adjoint.lean shows the 15 `(T : E →L[𝕜] F)` declarations between `namespace ContinuousLinearMap` (52/110/205/288) and their `end`s; the baseline line for that file is `TauCeti/Analysis/Fredholm/Adjoint.lean\t["TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_adjoint"]`. TauCeti/Analysis/Fredholm/Index.lean has no baseline line at all despite `noncomputable def index (T : E →L[𝕜] F)` at line 52 under `namespace TauCeti`/`namespace ContinuousLinearMap`.
findings.fix: Recognise the standard bundled-hom/equiv notations as their namespaces (map `→L[`→ContinuousLinearMap, `→ₗ[`→LinearMap, `≃L[`→ContinuousLinearEquiv, `≃ₗ[`→LinearEquiv, `→*`→MonoidHom, `→+*`→RingHom, `→ₐ[`→AlgHom, `≃`→Equiv, `≃*`→MulEquiv, `C(`→ContinuousMap, ...) instead of rejecting every binder type with a top-level arrow, then regenerate the baseline. Add a policy test using `(T : E →L[𝕜] F)` in `namespace ContinuousLinearMap` — the current tests only exercise types spelled `Foo`, so they cannot catch this.
findings.issue: `_binder_has_type` returns False whenever the binder type contains a top-level connective (`TOP_LEVEL_CONNECTIVES` includes `→`, matching `→L[𝕜]`, `→ₗ[R]`, `→*`, `→+*`) and also requires the type to be spelled with the namespace as a literal head. Mathlib receiver types are almost always written with notation, so the lint misses them. In TauCeti/Analysis/Fredholm/Adjoint.lean, 15 declarations in `namespace TauCeti`/`namespace ContinuousLinearMap` take an explicit `(T : E →L[𝕜] F)` (lines 60, 74, 95, 140, 148, 174, 186, 195, 209, 221, 231, 240, 250, 259, 292) and only one is in the baseline; TauCeti/Analysis/Fredholm/Index.lean, which defines `TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index (T : E →L[𝕜] F)` and six lemmas, is absent from the baseline entirely. The check the PR enables therefore lets through the majority of new violations of exactly the kind it targets, and grandfathers the existing ones by silence rather than by baseline entry.

findings.evidence: TauCeti/Analysis/Fredholm/Adjoint.lean:292 `theorem index_adjoint (T : E →L[𝕜] F) (hT : ContinuousLinearMap.IsFredholm T)`. Tracing `_binder_has_type`: `T`'s type fails on the `→` connective check (line 378), while `hT`'s type matches `(?:[\w']+\.)*ContinuousLinearMap\b` with remainder `.IsFredholm T`, which `\.[a-z_]` does not reject.
findings.fix: Treat a match as a receiver only when the remainder after the namespace name is empty or starts with whitespace/a closing delimiter — i.e. reject any dotted continuation, not just lowercase ones — and cover it with a test (`(h : Foo.IsBar x)` in `namespace Foo` must not be flagged).
findings.issue: The head-match only rejects a lowercase continuation (`re.match(r"\.[a-z_]", ...)`), so a binder whose type is `Ns.SomeCapitalizedThing x` counts as an argument of type `Ns`. This contradicts the module docstring's "explicit argument of the corresponding type" and flags declarations that have no dot-notation receiver at all: `TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_adjoint` is in the baseline solely because of `(hT : ContinuousLinearMap.IsFredholm T)` — a `Prop` in the sub-namespace, not a `ContinuousLinearMap`. Since scripts/ is base-owned and is not overlaid at PR time (pr-build.yml overlays only TauCeti/), a PR tripped by such a spurious finding cannot update the baseline to clear it.

summary: The receiver test does not implement the criterion the lint documents: it rejects any binder whose type contains a top-level arrow, so Mathlib's notation-spelled receivers (`E →L[𝕜] F`, `→ₗ[R]`, `≃`, `→*`) are never detected, and it accepts binders whose type head is `Ns.Something`, so declarations with no argument of type `Ns` are flagged. Both are demonstrable on the current tree, and the regenerated baseline is therefore not the census the PR presents it as.
